title: Cap. III Sol. Rat. 4: Jesuits vs other Pontificii — Mary/Apostles absolute; Valentia
pass_a_gloss: But let us also add this, that the Jesuits differ on this from other Pontificians; who teach that the virgin Mary, the blessed Apostles, and other eminently holy ones, were absolutely predestined to glory before all foresight of merits: And it is probable that the best were predestined in the best mode. Of those eminently holy ones, therefore, Valentia writes thus: Such, before the regard of the divine foresight to their final cooperation, are predestined to eternal life, On 1. q. 23. But let us leave the Jesuits fighting among themselves:
pass_b_english: Add also: the Jesuits themselves diverge here from other Roman doctors, who teach that the virgin Mary, the blessed Apostles, and other eminently holy persons were absolutely predestined to glory before any foresight of merits — and it is likely the best were predestined in the best way. Of those eminently holy ones Valentia writes: such are predestined to eternal life before any regard of God’s foresight to their final cooperation (In 1. q. 23). But leave the Jesuits fighting one another:
source_text: Sed illud etiam adjungamus, Jesuitas hunc ab aliis Pontificiis diffidere; qui virginem Mariam, beatos Apostolos, aliosque eximie sanctos, ad gloriam absolute praedestinatos docent ante omnem praescientiam meritorum: Verisimile autem est optimos fuisse optimo modo praedestinatos. De illis igitur eximie sanctis sic scribit Valentia, Tales ante respectum Divinae praescientiae ad finalem eorum cooperationem, praedestinantur ad vitam aeternam, In 1. qu. 23. Sed linquamus Jesuitas compugnantes:
